subject: Food Science
title: Supertasters and Non-Tasters
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Supertasters and Non-Tasters.

hook.text: 25% of people are 'supertasters' with twice the normal taste bud density. Broccoli, coffee, and grapefruit taste overwhelmingly.

buildup.text: Taste sensitivity is genetic, linked to the TAS2R38 gene. Supertasters have more fungiform papillae per square centimeter on.

discovery.text: The PROP test reveals tasting status: supertasters find the chemical intensely bitter. Non-tasters (also 25%) barely detect it.

twist.text: Supertasters tend to avoid vegetables (too bitter) and eat less variety. Ironically, heightened taste can lead to a less healthy.

climax.text: The remaining 50% are medium tasters. Most chefs and food critics fall here—sensitive enough to evaluate, not so sensitive they.

punchline.text: Your genes decide how intensely you taste. More isn't always better—balance matters.

quiz.question: What percentage of people are supertasters?
options: 25%—with twice the normal taste bud density
